releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.20
releasesInRange.body:
pnpm 12.20.0 records the specifiers of local directory dependencies in the experimental v13 lockfile and fixes several `nodeLinker: hoisted`, peer dependency, and `overrides` bugs. The bundled `node-gyp` no longer ships the undici version that security scanners flag. Remote resolution and shared build caches no longer work with pnpr 0.1.0-alpha.19 or older.

### Minor Changes

- With `lockfile.format: v13`, `pnpm install` records the dependency specifiers of local directory packages. Frozen installs reject changed specifiers even when the locked versions still satisfy them.

### Patch Changes

#### Upgrading and security

- Remote resolution, shared build caches, and release notes no longer work with pnpr 0.1.0-alpha.19 or older. pnpm now reads the capabilities a pnpr server advertises under `pnpr.protocols`. Installs fail when the server does not confirm the requested resolution and verification policies.

- The `node-gyp` bundled with pnpm no longer ships undici 6, which security scanners flag for CVE-2026-84947. On Node.js 26, `node-gyp` downloads through a proxy or with a custom CA file no longer crash with "invalid onError method" [#17941](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17941).

#### Resolving dependencies

- Version-selector `overrides` entries such as `"ms@^2.0.0": "2.1.1"` now apply to dependencies declared with the `catalog:` protocol when the catalog entry's range matches the selector [#17922](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17922).

- A root `overrides` entry that points a package at a `workspace:` path, such as `workspace:./packages/foo`, now also applies when a registry package depends on that package [pnpm/tasks#270](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/270).

- Git dependencies now accept npm's `::` separator between fragment parameters, such as `github:owner/repo#v1.0.0::path:packages/foo`. Before, pnpm read the whole fragment as a branch name and failed to resolve it [#17827](https://github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/17827).

- `pnpm dedupe` now keeps a locked runtime version, from `devEngines.runtime` or from a dependency's `engines.runtime`, when the declared range still admits it. `pnpm dedupe --check` no longer fails each time a newer Node.js release in the range comes out [#17984](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17984).

- With `autoInstallPeersFromHighestMatch`, conflicting non-semver peer dependencies now remain missing, and identical non-semver peer specifiers are preserved. Preferred registry versions no longer replace local paths or protocol-prefixed specifiers when pnpm installs missing peers [pnpm/tasks#272](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/272).

#### Hoisted node linker

- With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, a package now keeps its nested copy of a dependency that it resolved at a version other than the top-level one, including a peer dependency its parent supplies. Before, pnpm could remove that copy as a duplicate or give the top-level slot to a peer variant found deeper in the graph. The package then load
…(truncated)

prs.title: feat(pnpr): invalidate Cloudflare caches after registry changes
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Add pnpr-driven Cloudflare cache invalidation so anonymous public metadata and tarball cache hits do not contact the registry. Hosted package changes enqueue package purges atomically with their database writes. Runtime policy changes enqueue a deployment-wide purge. Pending deliveries survive restarts, and acknowledgements preserve concurrent mutations. An indexed queue prioritizes global policy purges and then the oldest package changes. A schema migration adds the index.

The Cloudflare example caches entries for at most five minutes from the start of the origin request, without stale fallback. This bounds failed purges and cache fills racing with mutations. Authenticated requests and private responses bypass shared caching. The guide documents setup and eventual access revocation.

Related to https://github.com/zkochan/pnpm-tasks/issues/56. This supplies the pnpr support and matching Worker example; applying it to the existing deployment requires the new pnpr version, a Cloudflare zone token, and the Worker update.

Validation: 2,322 affected Rust tests and 23 CLI smoke tests passed. The CDN tests cover queue persistence, concurrent acknowledgements, policy and artifact changes, token validation, and tarball cache headers. All 141 Cloudflare example tests and 23 MySQL schema/CDN tests passed. After the final fixes, all 251 selected configuration, CDN, hosted tar, and release-record tests passed. The final secret-validation refinement also passed all 240 config

prs.title: fix(pnpr): refuse deleting OCI child manifests referenced by retained indexes
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
### Why

Fixes zkochan/pnpm-tasks#48.

When an OCI image index (or Docker manifest list) is published to `pnpr`, [`OciPublication::stage`](pnpr/crates/pnpr/src/server/oci/publication.rs) checks `refuse_missing_children` so an index can only land if every child manifest it lists is retained in the repository's `ImageDocument`. However, `DELETE /v2/<name>/manifests/<digest>` previously called `ImageDocument::remove_manifest` without checking whether any retained index in the repository referenced the target digest. Deleting a child manifest by digest succeeded (`202 Accepted`) and left the tagged index pointing at a missing child (`404 MANIFEST_UNKNOWN` on platform pulls).

### How

1. **Record child digests on index `ManifestEntry` records**: Added `children: Vec<Digest>` (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`) to `ManifestEntry` in `pnpr-oci` and populated it during `OciPublication::stage` from the deduplicated `referenced` digests when `media_type::is_index(self.manifest.media_type())`.
2. **Enforce child retention in `ImageDocument::remove_manifest`**: Replaced the boolean return of `ImageDocument::remove_manifest` with `ManifestRemoval` (`Removed`, `NotFound`, `ReferencedByIndex`). If any other manifest in `self.manifests` contains `digest` in `children`, `remove_manifest` leaves the document untouched and returns `ManifestRemoval::ReferencedByIndex`.
3. **Answer `403 Forbidden` (`DENIED`) on `DELETE /v2/<name>/manifests/<digest>`**: Updated `Request::

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes https://github.com/zkochan/pnpm-tasks/issues/44

`pnpm/pnpm#17928` added 5 s idle stream eviction and stale-stream retry to `ConnectionPool::read` and `ConnectionPool::write`, covering `LibsqlAuth` and health/readiness endpoints.

`LibsqlAdapter` (`pnpr-sql`) checks out connections directly via `ConnectionPool::checkout` and runs metadata reads and writes across two or more Hrana batches in a transaction. When `sqld` or Turso expired a stream (`STREAM_EXPIRED`) or dropped/restarted its baton (`"Received an invalid baton"`) mid-transaction, metadata reads (without `replicaPath`) and metadata writes still failed instead of retrying on a fresh connection.

This PR:
- Exposes `pnpr_libsql::is_stale_stream` and `ConnectionPool::checkout_fresh` (evicting idle connections before opening a new stream, deduplicating `ConnectionPool::write`).
- Retries primary `LibsqlAdapter::read` (`!local`, bounded by the read's remaining `OPERATION_TIMEOUT` deadline) and uncommitted `LibsqlAdapter::write` (`StreamState::LostBeforeCommit`) once via `checkout_fresh` when `is_stale_stream` matches, while refusing to replay `Adapter::write` callbacks if an earlier batch in the callback already committed (`StreamState::Committed` -> `StreamState::LostAfterCommit`).

prs.title: fix(pnpr): honor npm 12 token permissions, day expiries, and restriction rejections
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes `pnpr`'s `POST /-/npm/v1/tokens` handling for npm 12 `npm token create` requests:

- **Permissions:** npm 12 omits classic `readonly` and sends `packages_and_scopes_permission`. `pnpr` now maps `"read-only"` to `readonly: true` and `"read-write"` to `readonly: false`, continues accepting classic `readonly: true | false`, and rejects conflicting combinations or unsupported permission modes (`"read-write-stage-only"`, `"no-access"`) with `400 Bad Request`.
- **Day expiries:** npm 12 sends `expires` as an integer day count (`parseInt(expires, 10)`). `pnpr` now treats positive integer `expires` values (and digit strings) as days (`days * 86_400` seconds) instead of seconds, keeps RFC 3339 timestamps on `expires` and seconds on `expires_in`, rejects specifying both or overflowing four-digit-year RFC 3339 timestamps, and resolves relative expiry timestamps after password verification so bcrypt latency does not eat into short `expires_in` TTLs.
- **Fail-closed granular restrictions:** Rejects fields `pnpr` cannot enforce (`packages`, `scopes`, `orgs`, `orgs_permission`, `packages_all: false`, and unknown fields via `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`) with `400 Bad Request` before password verification instead of silently minting an unrestricted token. Compatible npm 12 fields (`name: null`, `description`, `packages_all: true`, `bypass_2fa`) are accepted.

Closes https://github.com/zkochan/pnpm-tasks/issues/45

prs.title: fix(meta-updater): sync tsconfig references from manifests
prs.author: snmsoodan
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/309.

**Root cause:** The v11 lockfile reader converts the format-13 main document into an object with no `importers`. The updater then returns every tsconfig unchanged. With an older lockfile, references follow stale recorded dependencies rather than manifest edits.

**Repro:** After compiling the updater on unchanged main:

```sh
cd .meta-updater
../node_modules/.bin/node -e "import('@pnpm/lockfile.fs').then(async m => console.log(Object.keys((await m.readWantedLockfile('..', { ignoreIncompatible: false })).importers).length))"
```

Observed output: `0`.

Before the fix, `node_modules/.bin/node --test .meta-updater/test/tsconfig.test.mjs` failed: format-13 references were `undefined`, dependency removal retained an old v9 reference, and an absent lockfile threw `no lockfile found`.

**Fix:** Derive references from the workspace manifests already discovered by the updater. Reuse `WorkspaceSpec` for aliases and relative paths. Include local workspace peers, preserve existing cycle and outside-workspace exclusions, omit optional dependencies, and skip self references. Replace the private updater's lockfile dependency with the workspace-spec parser. Register the regression tests with the existing non-Jest CI dispatcher. Register `tsconfig.lint.json` and `test/tsconfig.json` as meta-updater callbacks, so `meta-updater --test` reports a stale generated config instead of rewriting it.

**Evidence:** Commands used pnpm 12.19.0

prs.author: kairosci

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Require flat registry declarations directly under `registries:`. Hosted and upstream registries select their protocol through `ecosystem:`. Nested ecosystem groups now fail configuration loading, eliminating the shape-dependent hosted `org` default.

Per-ecosystem `defaultRegistry` entries select existing targets and validate their protocols. Mixed routers and the shared default remain supported. Registry names are unique across the configuration.

```text
Remove the untagged flat-or-group registry parser and ecosystem-group
flattening. Grouping a hosted registry implicitly changed its org from
the default namespace to the registry name, hiding previously stored
packages. Accepting one declaration form removes that ambiguity.

Keep ecosystem selection on concrete registry entries. Per-ecosystem
defaults refer directly to those entries or routers without qualifying
names or assigning protocols. Existing flat namespace defaults remain
unchanged. Update the configuration docs and convert grouping fixtures
while retaining routing, publishing, cache, and managed-rule coverage.
```

prs.title: fix(pnpr): consolidate capability discovery on v0
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Consolidates pnpr capability discovery under `pnpr.protocols` and keeps `/v0/` as the supported HTTP protocol path. Disabled protocols advertise empty versions and features, and artifacts, compiler cache, and pipeline entries identify their experimental status. Discovery also works relative to npm registry bases and advertises only protocols reachable from that base.

The Rust client and TypeScript shared-cache client read the same map. Project transforms use the resolver feature list before sending a request. The duplicate flat lists, top-level feature flags, singular version fields, and response capability header are removed together while pnpr is pre-1.0. Server and client upgrades must ship together.

Closes https://github.com/zkochan/pnpm-tasks/issues/68.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Freeze capability discovery under pnpr.protocols with per-protocol versions,
features, and experimental status. Derive enabled capabilities from server
configuration and expose discovery at the root and npm registry bases.

Retain the v0 HTTP path used by released clients. Document version selection,
unknown-key handling, document-format versions, and future deprecation rules.
Update the Rust and TypeScript capability consumers together. Check project
transforms before sending a resolve request and remove the response header.

Closes https://github.com/zkochan/pnpm-tasks/issues/68.
```

prs.title: fix(pnpr): bound an upstream's credential by its packages claim
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

When pnpr's resolver chose a server-owned upstream credential for a fetch, `select_alias` matched the fetch by origin. It also checked the alias `access` and the per-package access rules. It never checked the upstream's `packages:` claim. A caller who sent `registry: https://npm.corp.example/` therefore got the corp token attached to fetches of any name on that host, and the metadata ended up in the returned lockfile.

`pnpr/docs/configuration.md` already promises that a `packages:` namespace bounds the credential ("a caller can't pull arbitrary public names through it"). The `/npm/~<name>/` endpoint enforced this. The resolver's origin path did not.

`upstream_admits` now also requires the registry graph to resolve the name to that upstream (`Registries::resolve` returns `Concrete`), in the ecosystem the upstream serves. Every alias-selection path goes through this check:

- origin fetches (`select_alias`);
- `/~<name>/` endpoint fetches;
- default-registry fetches;
- replays of a cached resolution's access descriptor (`allows_descriptor`).

The check uses the upstream's own ecosystem, not npm. The cargo and PyPI resolvers share this route hook and pass canonical crate and project names.

Because a claim can now steer which of several same-origin aliases is selected, a cache descriptor keeps its package whenever an earlier alias on that origin does not claim it. Without the package, a replay would re-select the earlier alias and the cached resolution would never 
…(truncated)

fix(pnpr): default npm publish rule to $owners
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

On npm registries, a `packages:` entry without a `publish` list fell back to `$authenticated`. Any signed-in account could publish a new version of another account's package and move its dist-tags. This makes `$owners` the npm default, so the first publish claims a name and later publishes and dist-tag moves need a maintainer or an `auth.admins` account.

Cargo, PyPI, and OCI publishes are authorized without reading maintainers, so `$owners` would admit nobody there. Those registries keep `$authenticated`. Config loading and the admin rules API now reject `$owners` in their rules, which replaces a silent deny-all with an error.

`$owners` is now listed in the access-token table in `pnpr/docs/configuration.md`, and the examples no longer write `publish: $authenticated`.

The registry-mock fixture config and preset set `publish: $authenticated` explicitly, so the pnpm test suites keep their current behavior.

Making `$owners` the default also exposed a check-then-lock window. Publish authorization ran before the package lock, so two accounts could both pass the "new name" check, and the second publish merged onto the package the first had just claimed. `stage_publish` now repeats the decision against the packument it read under the lock, with no extra read. Dist-tag changes authorize under the lock. The org package listing now evaluates `$owners`, so maintainers see "write".

Follow-ups, tracked separately:

- zkochan/pnpm-tasks#96: a dist-tag change on one replica

prs.author: zkochan

`pnpm deploy` can replace an injected workspace package's resolved dependencies with those of its workspace project. For a dependency that is also a peer, this can introduce a provider absent from the source installation. Each deployment must preserve the source dependency tree and peer bindings, survive a clean frozen reinstall without changing its lockfile, and reject a changed manifest. Add focused TypeScript regressions for both directory forms.

Related to pnpm/tasks#221. This follows pnpm/pnpm#17957 and covers the deploy oracle portion. Fast-update coverage and broader peer-decision consolidation remain separate work.

Deploy converts resolved package snapshots before synthesizing entries from
workspace importers. Both can produce the same file dependency key, but their
children belong to different peer contexts. Overwriting the resolved entry
with the importer can introduce a dependency that was absent in the source.

prs.title: refactor(pnpr): drop a comment that restates the blob path type
fix: accept npm's `::` separator in git dependency fragments
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Git dependencies now accept npm's `::` separator between fragment parameters, in both the TypeScript and the Rust CLI:

```sh
pnpm add 'gitlab:gitlab-org/cli#v1.124.0::path:internal/commands'
pnpm add 'github:owner/repo#semver:^1.0.0::path:packages/foo'
```

Before, pnpm only split the fragment on `&`. It read `v1.124.0::path:internal/commands` as one ref and failed with "Could not resolve ... to a commit".

Related to https://github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/17827.

Verification:

prs.title: feat(pnpr): add default and maximum token lifetimes
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds two pnpr settings for how long a token from a password login (`PUT /-/user/{name}`) or `POST /-/npm/v1/tokens` stays valid:

- `auth.tokens.defaultLifetime` (default `90d`): the lifetime of a login token, and of a created token that doesn't send `expires` or `expires_in`. Previously such tokens never expired. A created token can still ask for a different expiry.
- `auth.tokens.maxLifetime` (no default): a hard limit. A token created with a later expiry is shortened to the maximum. This uses the same mechanism as the existing cap that holds a passwordless token to its caller's expiry (`ValidatedTokenRequest::expiring_by`). The response's `expires` shows the shortened value.

Both must be at least `1m`, and a shorter or unparsable value fails config loading. OIDC browser sessions already expire within an hour, so neither setting applies to them.

Behavior change for operators: password-login tokens and created tokens without an expiry now stop working after 90 days. A CI secret made with `npm token create` and no expiry needs rotating, or the token can be created with an explicit `expires`. Tokens issued before this change keep their stored expiry.

This was the optional item left over from the pnpr web login hardening (pnpm/pnpm#17970).

`pnpm store add <file.tgz>` (pnpm/pnpm#17409) prepares the store for `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile`, but only for registry packages. It keys each tarball under the ids its manifest reveals, `<name>@<version>` and the registry-prefixed forms. A lockfile entry whose id is a URL never matches, so the offline install still fails with `ERR_PNPM_NO_OFFLINE_TARBALL` for:

- a dependency on a tarball URL, such as `is-odd@https://registry.yarnpkg.com/is-odd/-/is-odd-3.0.1.tgz`;

Sandboxed builders such as flatpak-builder-tools and Nix download these the same way as registry tarballs. Today they have to write pnpm's store rows themselves to serve them.
